Hoy, Miguel Parra-Hernandez está un paso más cerca para obtener la justicia que merece. La decisión del gran jurado envía un mensaje claro a nuestra comunidad: en un momento en que tantas cosas parecen estar fuera de nuestro control y cuando nuestras comunidades se sienten amenazadas, nos recuerda que nadie está por encima de la ley.

Tenemos que seguir exigiendo justicia para Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Renee Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero y por las familias y comunidades que aún no saben de sus seres queridos.

ICE tiene que rendir cuentas. Y todos los agentes que violan la ley deben responder ante la justicia, como cualquier otra persona. Tener la placa de identificación no le da derecho a ningún oficial de ICE actuar por encima de la ley. La justicia debe ser igual para todos, sin excepciones ni favoritismos.

Agradezco al fiscal del condado de Harris, Sean Teare, y a todo su equipo por su trabajo para que se haga justicia en este caso. Hoy damos un paso adelante, pero todavía queda mucho por hacer.

Today, Miguel Parra-Hernandez is one step closer to receiving the justice he deserves. The grand jury’s decision sends a powerful message to our community: even at a time when so much feels out of control, when our communities feel under attack, we are reminded that no one is above the law.

While today marks an important step toward justice in this case, our fight for accountability is far from over. We must continue demanding justice for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Renee Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, and so many others whose families and communities are still waiting for answers.

ICE must be held accountable, and officers who break the law must face justice in a court of law, just like anybody else. A badge does not place anyone above the law, and accountability cannot be selective.

I am grateful to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare and his team for their work in pursuing accountability in this case. Today is an important step forward, but our work is not done.

Me duele profundamente la muerte de Dolores Huerta. Nuestro país ha perdido a una gran luchadora por los derechos civiles, los derechos de los trabajadores y la justicia. Y he perdido a una querida amiga que me inspiró y a muchas otras personas de distintas generaciones. 

Yo crecí en Palito Blanco, Texas pizcando algodón en los campos bajo el sol caliente. Sé lo duro que es ese trabajo y los sacrificios que los trabajadores del campo y sus familias hacen todos los días. Dolores dedicó su vida a luchar para que los trabajadores fueran vistos y tratados con dignidad. Ella se enfrentó a los poderosos, organizó comunidades y luchó por salarios justos y mejores condiciones de trabajo para los que ponen la comida en nuestras mesas.

Ella era una feminista orgullosa y una gran defensora de los derechos de las mujeres. Dolores abrió el camino para latinas como yo. En una época cuando a las mujeres mexicoamericanas muchas veces les decían que se sentaran, que se hicieran a un lado y que se quedaran calladas, Dolores alzó la voz y nos demostró que nuestra voz importaba y que la gente común podía lograr cosas extraordinarias. 

Y siempre recordaré con una sonrisa que cada vez que Dolores venía a Houston, ella quería ir a un restaurante de Tex-Mex a comer carne guisada. Esos pequeños detalles eran parte de lo que la hacía tan especial para quienes la conocíamos. 

Mi corazón está con su familia, sus seres queridos y todas las personas a las que tocó con su vida. La mejor manera de honrarla es seguir luchando por la dignidad, la igualdad y la justicia, como ella lo hizo toda su vida. 

Descansa en paz, gran amiga. Seguiré la lucha que tú empezaste.

I am heartbroken by the passing of Dolores Huerta. Our country has lost a giant in the fight for civil rights, workers’ rights, and justice. And I have lost a dear friend who inspired me and countless others across generations.
 
I grew up in Palito Blanco, Texas, picking cotton in the fields under the hot sun. I know how hard that work is and the sacrifices farmworkers and their families make every day. Dolores dedicated her life to making sure those workers were seen, heard, and treated with dignity. She stood up to powerful interests, organized communities, and fought for  fair wages and better working conditions for the people who put food on our tables. 
 
She was also a proud feminist and a fierce champion for women’s rights. Dolores paved the way for Latinas like me. At a time when Mexican American women were too often told to sit down and stay quiet, Dolores stood up and showed us that our voices mattered and that ordinary people could accomplish extraordinary things. 
 
And I’ll always smile remembering how every time Dolores came to Houston, she wanted to go to a Tex-Mex restaurant for some carne guisada. Those are the little things that made her so special to those of us who knew her.

My heart goes out to her family, her loved ones, and the people whose lives she touched. We must honor her by continuing the fight for dignity, equality, and justice that she dedicated her life to.
 
Descansa en paz, gran amiga. Seguiré la lucha que tú empezaste.

The Trump administration says ICE is going after the “worst of the worst.” Apparently, that's who they're recruiting to be agents.

Today in Austin, I joined my colleagues to demand accountability for shootings by federal immigration agents across Texas.

In Houston, ICE shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a father of three with no criminal record who wasn't even their target. This lawlessness and cruelty cannot continue.

LIVE NOW: I'm participating in a congressional field hearing in Austin to examine ICE's reckless enforcement tactics, the harm they've caused our communities, and the urgent need for accountability.

The American people deserve answers. https://t.co/nWJoOeAbAT
@RepMonicaDLC 217 Members of Congress already put their constituents first and signed the discharge petition, what are you waiting for? https://t.co/cw3zjGd2Vr

Everything is bigger in Texas and thanks to Trump, so are gas and diesel prices. 
 
Gas prices are up from last year and diesel prices jumped to nearly $6 a gallon in Houston, the energy capital of the world.
 
Trump promised to lower prices on Day One. Instead, on Day 158, Americans are still paying more at the pump. 
 
This is unacceptable for working Americans, who feel the pain every time they fill up the tank.

Seniors will get about $75 more a month in Social Security next year to keep up with inflation.

Meanwhile, Trump's tariffs are costing families more than $1,000 a year, and his war in Iran is driving prices even higher.

Our seniors worked their whole lives to earn a dignified retirement. They deserve lower costs, not another bill they can't afford.

The numbers don’t lie. Americans have been feeling this pain at the gas pump, at the grocery store checkout, and when they pay their bills.

Trump’s “golden era” economy is only working for the rich, not everyday working Americans who are struggling to make ends meet. https://t.co/D2Gc15k1ox

Had a wonderful time at the San Jacinto College Police Department’s National Night Out! 

From connecting with families and sharing community resources to enjoying face painting and fun activities, it was a great evening bringing TX-29 together. 

Thank you to everyone who helped make this event special!
I'm keeping Pope Leo in my prayers and wishing him a speedy recovery. https://t.co/PFy91CjOdJ

This morning I met with the @USCIS Houston Field Office to discuss policy changes and find ways to strengthen our relationship. 

Through open communication and collaboration, we can build stronger partnerships to better serve the needs of TX-29. https://t.co/9kgfoWc1YD

I had a productive meeting with CRECEN Houston to hear directly from TPS holders about the challenges impacting our immigrant community in TX-29.

I will continue fighting to bring my American Dream and Promise Act discharge petition to the House floor and provide protections for TPS and DED holders, as well as DACA recipients. 

Immigrants are an essential part of what makes TX-29 rich in culture and opportunity. We cannot turn our backs on our neighbors or family.

This morning, I attended the Humanities Texas Outstanding Teaching Award Presentation to celebrate TX-29’s own Nikolai Burgardt, who is being recognized with an Award for Outstanding Early-Career Teaching. 

Our educators play a vital role in shaping the future of our communities. I will continue to support and honor our teachers at every opportunity. 

Congratulations to Mr. Burgardt on this well-deserved recognition!

The raid orchestrated by the Trump Administration is an abhorrent abuse of power.

No president should ever use the power of the federal government to threaten, silence, or intimidate political opponents, ever. Federal agencies exist to serve the American people, not to be weaponized against those who speak out and challenge the administration. 

ICE continues to operate in our communities with little to no accountability. We cannot let more agencies follow suit or normalize this use of power to silence people. 

This administration must be held accountable. The American people deserve answers and transparency.

On Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we honor the rich history, traditions, and contributions of Native communities here in Texas and across the country.

Indigenous Peoples have lived and flourished in the Americas for thousands of years. Their knowledge and cultures have helped shape our nation, and their contributions deserve to be recognized and celebrated.
I have been in touch with the Sheriff and will continue to monitor the situation.

An ICE vehicle struck a man during an enforcement operation in Harris County this morning. He’s now in the hospital.

We need to know exactly what happened, and ICE’s word alone is not enough. ICE has lied to the public before, and its operations have brought chaos to our communities.

Preserve the evidence. Cooperate fully with investigators. Give the public the answers it deserves.

It was a pleasure visiting Our Lady of Guadalupe Senior Center and spending time with the seniors who have given so much to our community. 

I’m making sure our seniors are informed and ready for Election Day! Remember, October 23 is the deadline to request a vote-by-mail application. 

Thank you for the warm welcome and for sharing your stories and concerns.

Congress gave DHS $20 million specifically for body cameras, yet ICE agents involved in shootings, including the killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in my district, weren't wearing them.

You don't get to carry a gun, take someone's life, and then dodge accountability.

No more excuses. No more hiding. We demand answers, and we demand accountability.
